issues.summary: The Maven scanner read the first <dependencies> element in each POM wherever it sat, which is not always the project's own dependency list. Two sets of POMs from Maven Central were compared with an XML parser on 2026-10-05. Neither is a random sample: the first is three pages of the search index and four group queries, the second is the dependency lists of two BOMs, parent POMs and hand-picked files, so the counts describe those sets. In the first, the scanner's dependency list differs on 87 of 420, each time reporting a dependency the POM does not declare. In the second it differs on 141 of 393. In that second set the XML parser finds a catalogued library in 23 POMs. The scanner flagged 26: 17 of those 23 and 9 that declare none. It missed the other 6. The Maven counts are wrong in both directions.

magnitude.unit: POMs in the second set whose dependency list the scanner read differently from an XML parser

Applying the scanner's own rule to the re-read data reproduces the published class for 28,914 of the 28,919 crates that could be re-read. issues.summary: The NuGet scanner counted a library that a package declares for only some of its target frameworks as a dependency of the package. Re-read from the NuGet registry on 2026-10-05 at the last version it lists for each package, which is the scanner's own rule: 1,905 of the 1,911 published entries could be read, and 87 of them match a catalogued library only in dependency groups for some target frameworks. Of the 200 re-read packages that remain weak-classed under the corrected classes, 57 declare the weak library that way, and 42 of the 57 belong to one family of packages whose names share their first part. Of the 1,702 re-read packages counted as modern-only, 36 match only that way. How far the re-read shows what the scan read depends on the date of that last version. For 721 packages it is dated before the scan, so the version is the one the scan read: among them the two counts are 2 of 63 and 14 of 656. For 1,047 it is dated after the scan, so the re-read is of a later version. The other 137 are unlisted, and the registry gives an unlisted version no date, so their date does not show which version the scan read: among them the counts are 51 of 65 and 1 of 72. A library is taken as declared for every target framework when it is in every dependency group of the package or in a group that names no framework.

magnitude.unit: published NuGet entries re-read on 2026-10-05 that match a catalogued library only in dependency groups for some target frameworks

issues.summary: A package whose metadata could not be read was still counted as scanned, and as using no cryptography. Each raw file records the number as fetchErrors: npm 5,374 of 1,000,000; PyPI 4,084 of 150,000; Go 76 of 200,117; Maven 26 of 103,400; Packagist 20,826 of 100,000; NuGet 6,855 of 100,000; CocoaPods 1 of 50,000. packagesScanned (2,170,994) therefore includes at least 37,242 packages that were not read, and withNoCrypto counts them as using no cryptography. The figure is a floor: in the npm and NuGet scanners some failed reads are not added to fetchErrors. Packagist cause, from a seeded sample of 300 packages run on 2026-10-05: 46 had no tagged release, which the scanner treated as a failed fetch. NuGet cause: not verified. crates.io has no fetchErrors field; its scanner counted only crates it read, and its file records 12 parse errors. RubyGems, Hex and pub.dev report 0. The Hex scanner counted a package only once it had read it, and the RubyGems and pub.dev scanners added every failed request to fetchErrors. Whether any pub.dev answer came without a pubspec, which that scanner counted as scanned and not as a failure, has not been verified.

magnitude.unit: packages counted as scanned that were not read (at least)

issues.summary: The catalogue's weak tier mixes libraries that implement broken algorithms with libraries that are deprecated or unmaintained, and it holds entries that the corrected classes do not class as weak. Re-aggregated on 2026-10-05 under the corrected classes, the 12,465 packages counted as depending on a weak library become between 10,749 and 10,809. Counting every package with a weak match, the published figure is 12,488: it adds the 23 that are filed as post-quantum because they also have a post-quantum match (21 crates, 2 npm packages). On that count the corrected figure is between 10,770 and 10,830. It adds 21 of the 23, the crates: under the corrected classes the two npm packages have no weak match. By ecosystem, on the published rule: npm 3,146 to 2,655; PyPI 201 to 173 or 174; Go 3,244 to 3,227; Maven 895 to 152; crates.io 4,460 to 4,266; Packagist 177 to between 61 and 86; NuGet 204 to 201; RubyGems 83 to between 4 and 37; CocoaPods 52 to 7 or 8; Hex and pub.dev do not change. A package that leaves the weak count and still matches another catalogued library moves to the modern-only count. The corrected classes count a library as weak only where it implements broken algorithms or an end-of-life signal was found. For 11 entries left out of the weak class no such signal was found either way and their status is not verified: tlslite (PyPI); bordoni/phpass and ircmaxell/random-lib (Packagist); CryptSharpOfficial (NuGet); crypt, gibberish and ezcrypto (RubyGems); crypto_dart (pub.dev); AESCrypt-ObjC, Arcane and CommonCryptoSwift (CocoaPods). 60 packages are counted as weak only through those entries: RubyGems 33, Packagist 25, PyPI 1, CocoaPods 1. That is why the corrected figures are ranges: the lower end takes none of the 11 as weak and the upper end takes all of them. On npm, Packagist and NuGet the unread packages work in the other direction and are unmeasured, so the net direction of weakExposed on those three rows is not established.

magnitude.unit: packages counted as depending on a weak library that remain so under the corrected classes; 10,809 if all 11 entries of unverified status are weak
